creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`./dev --doctor` shows two `scratch` daemons from the contract tier's smoke fixture
still running, one per smoke path, each holding one pane:

    60915  01-22:57:59  /private/tmp/muster-smoke/driving/config/herdr/...   scratch  1 pane
    61073  01-22:57:58  /private/tmp/muster-smoke/problems/config/herdr/...  scratch  1 pane

Two daemons, one per run of the tier, is exactly the shape `a_2I7ASgulK` describes and
was closed by `2a9c546`, "the contract tier ends every daemon it starts".

## The timing is what makes this worth filing

    fix committed      2026-09-03 08:17:43
    daemons started    2026-09-03 21:06:02

Thirteen hours after. So either the fix does not cover the path that run took, or that
run was made from a checkout without it.

## What has not been established

Nobody has reproduced it. Three explanations fit and they want different fixes:

- The tier was run from a worktree or checkout predating `2a9c546`. Would make this a
  non-issue, and is the first thing to rule out.
- The teardown runs on a normal exit and is skipped when the run is interrupted. A tier
  that needs a GUI session is one people stop with ctrl+c, so this is the explanation
  worth taking seriously.
- The teardown misses these two specifically. `driving` and `problems` are the smoke
  fixture's own paths rather than daemons the harness spawns, and the doctor's own note
  says what accumulates is "what a person or a fixture started outside" the harness.

## Cost, and why it is low priority

Twenty daemons together drew 0.1% CPU (`a_2I7ASgulK`), so this is not about speed. It is
that a stray daemon holding a live agent looks identical to one holding nothing, which is
the whole reason `./dev --doctor` exists. Every leak makes that list harder to read.

The two above are still running and safe to end - they hold one pane each in a temp home
under `/private/tmp/muster-smoke/`, not anybody's work.
title: 🧟 Two contract-tier daemons outlived the fix that was meant to end them
